Clarity.justification: The paper is well-structured with logical sections (Introduction, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Results, Discussion). The AS framework components (AS_loc, AS_state, AS_causal) and conditions (C1-C6) are clearly defined with regex patterns and tables. Minor issues include repetitive emphasis on the negative result without deeper analysis of alternatives.

Novelty.justification: The decomposition of feedback into localization/state/causal components is a modest conceptual contribution, but the core finding is a negative result on regex extraction feasibility (49.5% coverage) due to assertion errors (53.4% of failures). This documents a known boundary rather than advancing new methods or benchmarks substantially.

Soundness.justification: Methods (regex extraction, stratified sampling on 664 problems, 600 signals) are appropriate for the existence test (H-E1). Results match the provided code exactly (e.g., extraction rates: AS_loc 49.5%, AS_state 2.7%; ordering preserved on subset; correlations <0.5). No major flaws; the failure is transparently reported with root-cause analysis.

Significance.justification: Identifies a real issue (assertion errors lack traceback structure) relevant to LLM code repair, but the untested predictive power of AS and failure to meet the 95% extraction target limit impact. Contributions are primarily cautionary guidance rather than enabling new capabilities or lasting advances.

strengths: Clear identification of extraction barrier from assertion errors dominating benchmarks
Consistent experimental results matching provided code and preserving AS ordering on extractable subset
weaknesses: Negative result with low extraction rates undermines framework utility and novelty
Predictive power of AS untested due to operationalization failure, limiting broader significance
